{
  "claim": "recover_json_object skips duplicate-key JSON inside code fences instead of resolving duplicates last-wins, so it can return a later top-level object even though the rules say the last fenced object is scored when any fence holds one.",
  "expected": "For a fenced JSON object with repeated keys, recover_json_object should parse it using last-wins duplicate resolution, as it does for top-level candidates, and return that fenced object before considering later top-level objects.",
  "observed": "In the fenced pool, the except branch sets parsed = None when loads_strict fails, so a fenced candidate with duplicate keys is passed over. The function then proceeds to the top_level pool and returns a later top-level object that parses strict.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\":1,\"a\":2}\n```\n{\"b\":3}",
  "source_basis": "\"A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable\" and \"The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one\".",
  "execution_evidence": "none: no executable oracle",
  "scope": "Inputs whose last fenced JSON candidate contains repeated keys and is followed by a later top-level JSON object that parses strict JSON.",
  "uncertainty": "The defect assumes loads_strict refuses duplicate keys, which is explicit in the documentation and code comments. If loads_strict were permissive, the reproducer would not fail, but the code's strict-JSON branch implies refusal."
}
